implementation_notes: Rust's default realization of a part-whole tree is a recursive enum: the container variant holds Vec<Node> (or Box<Node> when the recursion is direct), which gives the type a finite size - recursive fields must sit behind a pointer - and every traversal becomes an exhaustive match. Ownership works in the pattern's favour here: a node has exactly one parent, dropping the root frees the whole tree, and the borrow checker makes two mutable paths to the same child impossible without Rc/RefCell, which is exactly the invariant a real tree wants. Use the trait-object variant when node kinds must be open to other crates.
pitfalls: A variant containing the enum directly (without Box/Vec) does not compile: the compiler reports a recursive type with infinite size.
Recursive traversal and recursive drop both use the stack, so very deep or untrusted trees need an explicit stack or an iterative destruction.
Adding a variant breaks every match without a catch-all - intentional, but it means visiting every traversal in the code base.

variants.name: Trait objects with Vec<Box<dyn Component>> (open node set)
variants.implementation_notes: For node kinds that the crate cannot enumerate - plugins, downstream implementations - Rust uses the trait-object realization: a dyn-compatible trait declares the uniform operation and containers hold Vec<Box<dyn Component>>, which lets heterogeneous nodes share one collection, exactly the shape the Book uses for a Screen of Draw components. Dispatch is dynamic through each fat pointer's vtable and every node is heap-allocated, and dyn-compatibility rules (no generic methods, no Self-returning methods) constrain the trait. Prefer the enum variant when the kinds are known; keep this one for genuine extensibility.
pitfalls: Each node is a separate heap allocation behind a fat pointer; the enum form is smaller and cache-friendlier for the same tree.
The trait must stay dyn-compatible: adding a generic method or a method returning Self silently makes Box<dyn Component> impossible.
Shared mutation across the tree needs Rc<RefCell<_>> or Arc<Mutex<_>>, trading compile-time aliasing checks for runtime panics or deadlocks.
